## NCBI CLI work

I looked up MeSH for environmental health, environmental exposure, environmental pollution, systematic reviews, meta-analysis, PRISMA, and quality assessment, along with methodological-quality and appraisal terms. I inspected the shortlisted descriptors and their entry terms and tree positions.

The environmental headings are tagged `[Mesh:noexp]` because their narrower headings include topics that could add noise, such as occupational, dietary, and war exposure. I included the entry terms from the selected descriptors as `[tiab]` variants. Lookup did not find an exact MeSH descriptor for methodological quality or critical appraisal; meta-analysis was considered but not included as a required concept.

PubMed tests returned **4,096** records for the review and environmental blocks together, and **1,031** after adding the methods block and date range. I checked the CLI’s query translations and fetched sample records. The sample included unrelated systematic reviews, so screening burden remains; no seed-PMID validation was possible because none were supplied.

These counts come from live PubMed CLI checks with the requested date range; they are not a reconstruction of PubMed’s database as it stood on July 20, 2020. Some sampled records show later issue years, which can occur for online-first records. Confirm how the review will handle online-first dates when applying the cutoff.

No language, species, or other limits were added. No separate validated filter was used. No post-cutoff literature was used to build the search.

## Peer review and caveats

This is a draft strategy. Have a second information specialist peer review it using PRESS before running it as the final search. PubMed is the only database covered here; the strategy will need translation for each additional database in the protocol. No seed validation was performed.
